title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only work at the document level (or on narrow, task-specific token tasks such as spell checking), so they cannot localize which tokens in a text are anomalous. The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, releases three token-annotated benchmarks (SMS_Spam with injected character corruption, Restaurant Review semantic anomalies, Grammar errors), and proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal word-level token embeddings (BERT-base-uncased embeddings aggregated by element-wise max pooling over subwords) and scores each test token by its nearest-neighbor distance, aggregating token scores by mean for document-level scores. TokenCore achieves the best average token-level AUROC (0.7145) and document-level AUROC (0.7335) among 7 methods, ranking first at token level on Review (0.8271) and Grammar (0.6371) and at document level on Review (0.9594), while ECOD/iForest remain better on the character-corruption SMS_Spam token-level task.

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction of claim C1: TokenCore's token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (0.6371, tolerance ±0.02 absolute). We clone the authors' repo, keep TokenCore.py/align.py/json_to_npy.py verbatim, and rebuild only the missing driver that Demo.ipynb used to hide: read the released grammar annotations (data/grammar_correction_labeled.json and data/grammar.npy), build the 300-document corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10), take 50% of the normal documents as the memory-bank training set (R6, A8), run BERT-base-uncased over the remaining normal + anomalous documents, max-pool subword embeddings into word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1, R2/R9, A3/A4), fit the authors' TextCore memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3, A2), score every test token by Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4, A1/A9), and compute pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC plus the mean-aggregated document-level scores (Eq. 3, R5, A5). The paper value is a single split-free number, so the only real drift risk is split randomness on 300 short documents; we therefore report a primary seeded run plus a small multi-seed spread so the ±0.02 band can be interpreted. Only the Grammar dataset is needed for C1, but the same driver is written so that running it on restaurant_review / sms_spam later costs nothing extra.

Run the intermediate checks (see intermediate_checks) before the full run.

    1| # TokenCore
    2| 
    3| Official code and datasets for the paper
    4| **[Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection](https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.13644)** (WWW '26).
    5| 
    6| TokenCore is a memory-bank method for **token-level text anomaly detection**: instead of only flagging whole documents as anomalous, it localizes *which specific tokens* are anomalous. It builds a memory bank of normal token embeddings and scores each test token by its distance to the nearest normal neighbor, then aggregates token scores to obtain document-level scores.
    7| 
    8| ## Datasets
    9| 
   10| The three benchmark datasets are hosted on the Hugging Face Hub:
   11| 
   12| 👉 **[https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD)**
   13| 
   14| Each dataset provides both document-level and token-level anomaly annotations.
   15| 
   16| | Dataset | Anomaly type | Documents | Anomalies | Rate |
   17| |---|---|---|---|---|
   18| | SMS Spam | Character-level (corrupted sequences) | 4,518 | 393 | 8.7% |
   19| | Restaurant Review | Semantic (negative sentiment) | 1,100 | 50 | 4.5% |
   20| | Grammar Correction | Grammatical errors | 300 | 30 | 10% |
   21|

   28| cd TokenCore
   29| pip install -r requirements.txt
   30| ```

   38|

def score_split(X, z, ptr, docs, seed):
    """One 50/50 split: fit memory bank on normal-train tokens, score test tokens."""
    from TokenCore import TokenCore  # authors' code, unmodified
    train_docs, test_docs = split_docs(docs, seed)
    tr_ids = set(id(d) for d in train_docs)
    tri = np.array([i for i, p in enumerate(ptr) if id(docs[p]) in tr_ids])
    tei = np.array([i for i, p in enumerate(ptr) if id(docs[p]) not in tr_ids])
    Xtr, Xte, zte, pte = X[tri], X[tei], z[tei], ptr[tei]
    assert z[tri].sum() == 0, "training set must contain zero anomalous tokens (R3)"
    assert Xtr.shape[1] == 768 and Xte.shape[1] == 768

    model = TokenCore(n_neighbors=1)  # full memory bank, nearest neighbor
    model.fit(Xtr)
    scores = model.decision_function(Xte)

    from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score
    tok_auroc = roc_auc_score(zte, scores)          # pooled micro over all test tokens (A5)
    tok_auprc = average_precision_score(zte, scores)

    # document-level: mean aggregation of token scores (Eq.3, R5)
    te_doc_pos = {id(d): j for j, d in enumerate(test_docs)}
    local_ptr = np.array([te_doc_pos[id(docs[p])] for p in pte])
    doc_scores = np.array([scores[local_ptr == j].mean() for j in range(len(test_docs))])
    doc_labels = np.array([d["doc_label"] for d in test_docs])
    doc_auroc = roc_auc_score(doc_labels, doc_scores) if doc_labels.sum() > 0 else float("nan")
    doc_auprc = average_precision_score(doc_labels, doc_scores) if doc_labels.sum() > 0 else float("nan")

    # A5 alternative, diagnostic only: mean of per-document token-level AUROCs
    per_doc_aurocs = []
    for j in range(len(test_docs)):
        m = local_ptr == j
        if 0 < zte[m].sum() < m.sum():
            per_doc_aurocs.append(roc_auc_score(zte[m], scores[m]))
    tok_auroc_perdoc = float(np.mean(per_doc_aurocs)) if per_doc_aurocs else float("nan")

    # sanity: random control
    rng = np.random.RandomState(123)
    rand_auroc = roc_auc_score(zte, rng.rand(len(zte)))

    return {
        "seed": seed,
        "n_train_docs": len(train_docs), "n_test_docs": len(test_docs),
        "n_bank_tokens": int(len(Xtr)), "n_test_tokens": int(len(Xte)),
        "n_positive_tokens": int(zte.sum()),
        "token_auroc": float(tok_auroc), "token_auprc": float(tok_auprc),
        "token_auroc_perdoc_mean": tok_auroc_perdoc,
        "doc_auroc": float(doc_auroc), "doc_auprc": float(doc_auprc),
        "random_control_auroc": float(rand_auroc),
        "positive_rate": float(zte.mean()),
    }

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score and the paper prints it in [0,1] as a fraction; no std/CI over repeated runs is reported (rule 1 inapplicable), and the token-level test set for Grammar is only ~150 documents' tokens, whose size is never stated as 2,000+ examples, so the smaller-set band of 0.02 absolute is used rather than the 0.01 of rule 2.

audit_summary: Reproduction targets C1 correctly: it loads the released 300-document Grammar benchmark (270 normal / 30 anomalous), applies the authors' TokenCore memory bank to max-pooled BERT word embeddings, scores tokens by nearest-neighbor Euclidean distance, and uses the required 50% normal-train / rest+anomalous test split. Core R2-R7 and R9-R11 are met; only R1 is partial because the backbone is bert-base-cased (released-repo default, A12) rather than the paper text's BERT-base-uncased, and R8 is missing because no baselines were run. The measured token AUROC is 0.6251 +/- 0.0243 over seeds 0-2 (seed 0 = 0.6583, per-seed range 0.601-0.658), which is within the +/-0.02 tolerance of the 0.6371 target; the document AUROC mean of 0.6578 also closely matches the paper's Grammar document AUROC of 0.6553. No reported number is hard-coded or echoed from the paper: target and tolerance are read from state/plan.json, and metrics are computed from fresh embeddings with a random-control AUROC of 0.569. The run is not scaled down -- full dataset, full normal-token memory bank, three seeds -- but the unreleased split seed (A13) and the paper-vs-repo backbone ambiguity (A12) are the main residual uncertainties. The Grammar-only scope means the multi-dataset averages (C5-C7) and baseline comparisons were not checked here.

requirement_check.evidence: reproduce.py uses BERT contextual embeddings with element-wise max pooling, but the backbone is bert-base-cased (metrics config; released-repo default, assumption A12) rather than the paper-stated BERT-base-uncased; baselines are also not run.
embed_docs groups subwords by word_ids and applies np.max(out[b, groups[wid], :], axis=0) per gold word; tail confirms 2746 word units x 768 aligned 1:1 with gold tokens.
TokenCore.fit(Xtr) uses only the 135 normal training docs; assert z[tri].sum()==0 checks no anomalous training tokens; bank sizes are 1202-1225 normal-token embeddings.
TokenCore(n_neighbors=1).decision_function(Xte) supplies the nearest-neighbor Euclidean distance; roc_auc_score(zte, scores) treats larger distance as anomalous and gives 0.6251 mean token AUROC.
Document scores are the mean of test-token scores per document (doc_scores = scores[local_ptr == j].mean()), then doc AUROC/AUPRC are computed.
split_docs permutes the 270 normal docs, takes the first 135 as train and the remaining 135 normal + all 30 anomalous as test; counts report 135 train / 165 test docs.
metrics.json reports token_auroc, token_auprc, doc_auroc and doc_auprc using sklearn roc_auc_score and average_precision_score.
No baseline code or runs; reproduce.py only imports and evaluates TokenCore, so LOF, iForest, ECOD, DeepSVDD, AutoEncoder and LUNAR are absent.
The embedding loop asserts len(order) == len(d['tokens']) for every document, ensuring one word-level vector per gold-token word unit.
